emptyResponseError: {{provider}} returned an empty response. This usually means the API is misconfigured (base URL, model, or credentials).

emptyResponseNoEvents: {{provider}} accepted the request but streamed no data at all. The upstream most likely dropped the response; if it keeps happening, check the base URL, model, and credentials.
emptyResponseUsageOnly: {{provider}} streamed only bookkeeping data (usage/queue) and no content. The request reached the model, so this is an upstream problem, not a local configuration error.
emptyResponseNamelessToolCall: {{provider}} announced a tool call without a tool name, so nothing could run. This is an upstream protocol fault.
emptyResponseStopWithoutContent: {{provider}} finished with "{{stopReason}}" but produced no content. The request reached the model, so this is an upstream problem, not a local configuration error.
reasoningOnlyExhausted: {{provider}} kept returning reasoning without an answer or tool call. This is a model-behaviour problem — try a different model or simplify the task.
cyberPolicyViolation: {{provider}} refused this request under its cyber-security policy (cyber_policy). The turn was terminated without retrying or switching accounts; sending similar content again may get the upstream account banned.

dangerCopy_shellAnalysisFailedC1: NarraFork could not inspect the command before execution.
dangerCopy_shellAnalysisFailedC2: In Bypass All mode, executing an unanalyzed shell command may modify files, run code, or access external paths without an effective safety gate.
dangerCopy_shellAnalysisFailedA1: Retry after fixing the command analysis failure.
dangerCopy_shellAnalysisFailedA2: Break the task into dedicated read/write tools or smaller explicit commands.
dangerCopy_shellAnalysisFailedA3: Run only after the visible command has been manually verified as intentional and bounded.
dangerCopy_planRelaxSummary: Plan mode is about to be relaxed for a non-planning tool call.
dangerCopy_planRelaxC1: The narrator is still in plan mode, but this approval will enable relaxed plan mode so edit-capable tools can run.
dangerCopy_planRelaxC2: Implementation changes may begin before the plan has gone through the normal plan-mode approval path.
dangerCopy_planRelaxA1: Continue read-only investigation and write only to the designated plan file.
dangerCopy_planRelaxA2: Submit the complete plan first, then run implementation tools after approval.
dangerCopy_gitResetSummary: Git reset may rewrite the current worktree/index state.
dangerCopy_gitResetC1: Uncommitted work can be discarded or unstaged.
dangerCopy_gitResetC2: HEAD/index changes can be hard to reconstruct without reflog or backups.
dangerCopy_gitResetA1: Run git status and git diff first.
dangerCopy_gitResetA2: Create a backup branch or stash before resetting.
dangerCopy_gitCleanSummary: Git clean removes untracked files from the worktree.
dangerCopy_gitCleanC1: Untracked files are often not recoverable from git.
dangerCopy_gitCleanC2: Generated artifacts, local notes, or new source files may be deleted.
dangerCopy_gitCleanA1: Run git clean -nd first to preview.
dangerCopy_gitCleanA2: Delete only specific paths if possible.
dangerCopy_gitCheckoutSummary: Git checkout is being used to restore paths and may discard local changes.
dangerCopy_gitCheckoutC1: Modified files can be reverted without preserving the previous content.
dangerCopy_gitCheckoutA2: Restore only the specific files that must be reverted.
dangerCopy_gitRestoreSummary: Git restore may discard local file changes.
dangerCopy_gitRestoreC1: Affected files can be reverted without preserving the previous content.
dangerCopy_gitRestoreA2: Restore only specific files rather than the whole tree.
dangerCopy_gitPushSummary: Git push may rewrite or delete remote history.
dangerCopy_gitPushC1: Remote commits or branches can be overwritten or removed for collaborators.
dangerCopy_gitPushC2: Recovery may require remote reflogs or manual intervention.
dangerCopy_gitPushA2: If force is necessary, verify the remote branch and use --force-with-lease.
dangerCopy_gitBranchDeleteSummary: Git branch deletion removes a local branch reference.
dangerCopy_gitBranchDeleteC1: Commits reachable only from that branch can become difficult to find.
dangerCopy_gitBranchDeleteA1: Check git branch --merged and note the commit hash before deleting.
dangerCopy_gitWorktreeSummary: Git worktree remove deletes a worktree checkout.
dangerCopy_gitWorktreeC1: Uncommitted files in that worktree may be lost.
dangerCopy_gitWorktreeA2: Commit, stash, or copy important files before removal.
dangerCopy_gitRmSummary: Git rm deletes tracked files from the worktree and index.
dangerCopy_gitRmC1: Files will be removed and staged for deletion.
dangerCopy_gitReflogSummary: Git reflog expire can destroy recovery points.
dangerCopy_gitReflogC1: Future recovery from accidental resets or rebases may become impossible.
dangerCopy_gitReflogA1: Avoid expiring reflogs during agent work unless explicitly required.
dangerCopy_gitStashDropSummary: Git stash drop permanently removes a stash entry.
dangerCopy_gitStashDropC1: The stashed changes cannot be recovered after dropping.
dangerCopy_gitStashDropC2: If the stash contains important uncommitted work, it will be lost.
dangerCopy_gitStashListFirst: Run git stash list first to inspect.
dangerCopy_gitStashDropA2: Apply the stash before dropping it.
dangerCopy_gitStashClearSummary: Git stash clear removes all stash entries.
dangerCopy_gitStashClearC1: All stashed changes will be permanently lost.
dangerCopy_gitStashClearC2: Recovery is not possible after clearing the stash.
dangerCopy_gitStashClearA2: Apply or pop important stashes before clearing.
dangerCopy_gitGcSummary: Git gc --prune can permanently remove unreachable objects.
dangerCopy_gitGcC1: Commits/files recoverable only via dangling objects may be deleted.
dangerCopy_gitGcA1: Avoid aggressive pruning during agent work.
dangerCopy_gitGcA2: Create a backup ref first if pruning is required.
dangerCopy_gitHistoryRewriteA2: Prefer a new commit if history rewriting is not required.
dangerCopy_gitHistoryRewriteC1: Commit hashes change and collaborators may need manual recovery steps.
dangerCopy_deleteFilesC1: Deleted files may not be recoverable from git if they are untracked or ignored.
dangerCopy_deleteFilesC2: The operation can remove user work that the agent did not create.
dangerCopy_deleteFilesA2: Prefer moving files to a temporary trash directory.
dangerCopy_findUnknownSummary: Find runs a command NarraFork could not classify.
dangerCopy_findUnknownC1: The executed command's side effects are unknown, and find applies it to every match.
dangerCopy_bypassC: In Bypass All mode this would otherwise execute without user approval.
dangerCopy_findUnknownA1: Run the same find command without -exec first to see what it would match.
dangerCopy_findUnknownA2: Invoke the command directly on explicit paths instead.
dangerCopy_findDestructiveSummary: Find is being used to delete files or run a destructive command.
dangerCopy_findMutatingSummary: Find applies a state-changing command to every match.
dangerCopy_findMutatingC1: It can affect many matching files at once, including files the agent did not inspect.
dangerCopy_findMutatingC2: Paths written through the find expression are not covered by the worktree boundary check.
dangerCopy_findMutatingA1: Run the same find command without -delete/-exec first.
dangerCopy_dangerousPatternsSummary: Shell command contains dangerous execution patterns.
dangerCopy_unclassifiedPatternsSummary: Shell command includes unclassified execution patterns.
dangerCopy_dangerousPatternsC1: The command may execute downloaded, nested, or environment-injected code.
dangerCopy_dangerousPatternsC2: Side effects may be broader than the visible command line suggests.
dangerCopy_unclassifiedPatternsC1: The command may execute a local script, unknown subcommand, or unallowlisted argument whose side effects are not classified.
dangerCopy_splitReadExecute: Break the command into read-only inspection and explicit execution steps.
dangerCopy_preferDedicatedTool: Use a dedicated NarraFork tool for read/write operations when possible.
dangerCopy_breakOrWhitelist: Break the command into smaller inspected steps or add a narrow command whitelist rule if this exact command is trusted.
dangerCopy_nonAllowlistedSummary: Shell command includes commands outside the safety allowlist.
dangerCopy_nonAllowlistedC1: The command may run code, invoke a package/script, change system state, or perform side effects that NarraFork cannot classify as read-only.
dangerCopy_shellExternalPathsSummary: Shell command accesses paths outside the current working directory.
dangerCopy_shellExternalPathsC1: The command may read or modify files outside this worktree boundary.
dangerCopy_shellExternalPathsC2: Those files may not be covered by NarraFork snapshots or git recovery.
dangerCopy_shellExternalPathsA1: Copy needed data into the worktree first.
dangerCopy_shellExternalPathsA2: Use a narrower command scoped to explicit paths.
dangerCopy_toolExternalPathsC1: The operation crosses the worktree boundary.
dangerCopy_toolExternalPathsC2: External files may not be covered by project git history or NarraFork snapshots.
dangerCopy_toolExternalPathsA1: Operate inside the worktree when possible.
dangerCopy_toolExternalPathsA2: Use explicit user approval for external files.
dangerCopy_switchCwdSummary: SwitchWorkingDirectory changes the narrator's execution workspace.
dangerCopy_switchCwdC1: Subsequent tools use a different working directory, skills and permission context.
dangerCopy_switchCwdC2: Existing background tools, subagents and terminals remain on their original targets.
dangerCopy_switchCwdA1: Verify the target device and directory match the user's requested workspace.
dangerCopy_switchCwdA2: Keep the current workspace if switching is not necessary for this task.
dangerCopy_subagentWorkdirSummary: Write-capable subagent requests a custom working directory.
dangerCopy_subagentWorkdirC1: The subagent may operate outside the parent narrator's current workspace.
